reason: "All of the above" option (d) with option a claiming drums reduce total weight -- drums divide weight into manageable sections but do not reduce total structural weight. Option a is misleading. Better to make each option independently verifiable and remove the catch-all. Replace with specific correct answer identifying easier transport and entasis as distinct benefits.

proposed.text: Greek temple columns were built using stone drums stacked vertically rather than monolithic shafts. Which of the following accurately describes a key advantage of this construction method?

options.text: The drums could be carved with precise entasis curves, and the modular sections were easier to transport and position than a single massive stone column
Stone drums increased the total weight of the column, improving structural stability against lateral forces like wind and earthquakes
The drums eliminated the need for entasis, as the stacked sections naturally self-corrected any visual distortion in the column profile
Each drum was carved as a complete column unit, allowing quick assembly by simply stacking the pre-finished sections on site

rationale.a: Correct. The article states: 'columns were built in drums (cylindrical sections) stacked vertically. Entasis...was achieved by subtle reductions in diameter between drums.' This modular approach also made transport and positioning easier than moving monolithic shafts.
rationale.b: Incorrect. Drums divide the weight into manageable sections for transport; total weight is unchanged. Columns are stacked, not heavier.
rationale.c: Incorrect. Entasis was still required and was achieved through the drum construction method, not eliminated by it.
rationale.d: Incorrect. Drums were individual sections stacked and aligned, not pre-finished complete column units. The column form emerged from the stacked assembly.
rationale.correct: Stacking drums served two purposes: (1) enabling entasis through controlled diameter reductions between sections, and (2) allowing manageable transport and positioning of individual stone sections compared to monolithic columns.
rationale.takeaway: Greek column drums served dual functions: structural modularity for construction and the means to achieve sophisticated optical refinements like entasis.
